title: The Hourglass That Bred More Hourglasses
story: In the Clockwright's vault, Mr 6 meets Grindlewatch: a walking hourglass that, every time a blade taps its glass, bursts into five smaller hourglasses — and every one of them starts counting down the village's remaining daylight. There are 3 of them humming on the shelf right now. Mr 6 lowers his sword and starts doing arithmetic instead.
question: If Mr 6 foolishly struck every hourglass once, and then struck every hourglass again, and then a third time — each strike turning one hourglass into 5 — how many hourglasses would be ticking after the third round?
solution: That would be 375 hourglasses — so Mr 6 wisely never swings at all.
praise: Multiplying by 5 for each round was the right engine — it just needed to run all three rounds, not stop early.
hint: Each round multiplies the whole group by 5. Start with 3 and do that three times in a row.
victory: Mr 6 announced "three hundred seventy-five" and sheathed his sword. Grindlewatch, who had never once been out-counted, sighed its sand out in defeat and became an ordinary, very punctual clock.
imagePrompt: A numeral-six knight stands calmly with sheathed sword in a candlelit clockwright's vault while a towering hourglass monster trembles amid shelves of glittering smaller hourglasses.
